question: Can a cheap model do the assistant's routing work (profile assignment) without degrading which profile a task lands on?
method: 12 real goals (experiments/e06-goals.txt) covering every lane; identical router prompt to 3 models in --oneshot mode; ground truth = lane assignments fixed a priori (documented below) before scoring. Note: this tests the ASSIGNMENT decision; the live kanban_decomposer slot outputs were already spot-checked in E06-F5.
verdict: deepseek-v4-flash (the F5 repin candidate) matches 11/12 vs baseline gpt-6-luna 12/12 and glm-5.3-flash 12/12 — the single disagreement is goal 11 (debug+fix task assigned main instead of advisor), a genuinely borderline call. Latency is the bigger cost: deepseek 21s vs luna 13s per batch. At ~$0.0005/batch for deepseek vs $0.000135 for glm, glm is both cheaper and as accurate here — and it is the main model already.
recommendation: For routing-slot repinning: deepseek-v4-flash is validated but adds ~60% latency; glm-5.3-flash is the better repin target if a slot needs a cheap model (accurate, cheapest). No live routing change made — this was an offline replica of the decision.
limitations: n=12 goals, one batch run per model (no repeats)
assignment tested offline, not the live decomposer latency
ground truth set a priori by one rater
